title: Infosys Opens 1.1 Million Sq Ft Block at Hyderabad Pocharam Campus
excerpt: The new Pocharam block adds 10,000 seats and aims to support more than 13,000 additional employees under a hybrid model across a 450-acre campus.
body:
• Infosys opened a new 1.1 million sq ft software development block at its Pocharam campus in Hyderabad on Friday.
  • The block adds 10,000 seats and aims to support more than 13,000 additional employees under a hybrid working model.
  • The 450-acre campus now has seven blocks with about 4.58 million sq ft of built-up area.
  • The centre serves global clients in banking and financial services, retail, life sciences and manufacturing, with work in AI, cloud, cybersecurity and engineering.

Infosys has expanded its Pocharam development centre in Hyderabad with a new 1.1 million sq ft software development block, adding 10,000 seats to the campus, The Hindu BusinessLine reported on Friday. Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka and IT and Industries Minister D Sridhar Babu inaugurated the block in the presence of Infosys Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka.

The News Trust reported the same inauguration in Hyderabad on October 30, saying the new block adds capacity for 10,000 workstations at the Pocharam Development Centre.

Scale of the Pocharam campus

The campus numbers explain why the expansion matters for delivery capacity. Spread over 450 acres, Pocharam now has seven software development blocks with a total built-up area of about 4.58 million sq ft, both outlets reported. With the additional seats, Infosys aims to support over 13,000 more employees under a hybrid working model, according to its statement quoted by BusinessLine.

https://x.com/Infosys/status/2116183345390407953

That distinction matters for readers tracking jobs. The physical addition is 10,000 seats; the workforce the company says it can support under hybrid working is more than 13,000, because not every employee is on site every day.

"This facility enhances our capacity to scale operations, build specialised talent, and deliver complex transformation programmes for global clients."

— Jayesh Sanghrajka, Chief Financial Officer, Infosys

What work the centre does

According to BusinessLine, the centre serves global clients in banking, financial services and insurance, retail, life sciences and manufacturing. The expansion would add to the company's work in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and digital services.

The News Trust gave a similar list, describing the expansion as strengthening capabilities in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services. It added detail on the building itself, saying the facility incorporates energy-efficient cooling systems, smart lighting, rainwater harvesting and wastewater reuse, besides flexible workspaces and employee wellness facilities.

Telangana's pitch

State leaders framed the opening as a Hyderabad story as well as a company story. Bhatti Vikramarka said the expansion would create opportunities for the state's youth to take part in "the next wave of technology-led growth," BusinessLine reported. The News Trust reported a similar comment, that Bhatti said the expansion reflected Hyderabad's growing status as a global technology destination.

For Indian technology professionals in the United States and elsewhere who work with Hyderabad delivery teams, a larger Pocharam base means more of that client work can be staffed from a single large campus rather than split across smaller sites. The company did not, in the reports, disclose a capital expenditure figure for the block or change earnings guidance in connection with the inauguration.

What to watch

The next test is utilisation: how quickly the 10,000 new seats fill under the hybrid model, and whether client demand in banking, retail, life sciences and manufacturing keeps pace with the added capacity. Infosys said the facility is intended to help it scale operations and build specialised talent, and hiring and project allocation over the coming quarters will show how that capacity is used.
